title: Habit loop KPI experiment — sprint scratchpad
content:
Sprint 5: habit-loop KPI experiment (scratchpad)
Owner: Jasper Chen — personal OKR thread
Collaborators: Maya P., Eliot M. (quick syncs)

Objective: establish a repeatable habit loop that increases meaningful output (core tasks closed) while keeping cognitive load low. Link back to my quarterly OKR: increase feature throughput by +15% contribution (measured as PRs merged where I own >50% of work) and reduce context-switch noise.

Key hypothesis:
- If I install a consistent cue->routine->reward loop (morning 10-min plan, 2x 90-min deep blocks, end-of-day 10-min micro-retro), then weekly meaningful output (M) will rise by at least 20% over baseline within 3 sprints without increasing weekly hours by >10%.

Primary metrics (how I measure success):
- M: number of meaningful tasks completed per week (defined: tickets with label 'owner:jasper' and merged PR) — baseline (Sprint 0): 3.
- F: Focus minutes per day (from Clockify and calendar blocked time) — baseline avg: 140 min/day.
- S: Streaks — number of consecutive weekdays where morning plan occurred. Baseline: 2.
- Cognitive load proxy (CL): number of context switches recorded in day-notes (>3/min indicates noisy day). Baseline: median 5/day.

Data sources / instrumentation:
- Clockify tags (personal-projects) + Calendar blocked events ("Focus — Jasper").
- GitHub PR labels and merge dates (automation: script pulls label owner:jasper).
- Lightweight daily note (this doc updated each evening) with quick counts and micro-retro bullets.
- Slack thread summary (post EOD weekly).

Planned interventions (Sprint 5) — simple, low-friction:
1) Morning ritual (10 minutes) — write top 3 outcomes, pick 1 anchor task (M1), set two focus blocks.
   - Cue: alarm + calendar pop-up at 9:10
   - Reward: small checklist tick + email to Maya about daily anchor (social accountability).
2) Two 90-min protected blocks (11:00–12:30, 14:00–15:30) — do not accept meetings; allow 1 async message check at block midpoint.
3) Micro-retros (10m) at EOD — capture: what moved, blockers, adjust tomorrow.
4) Weekly sync with Eliot on Friday 10:30 (10m) to compare notes and share tactics.

Week-by-week check-ins (quick logs)
- 2026-02-22 (Mon) — Day 1: morning ritual done (streak=1). Focus blocks mostly uninterrupted, clockify shows 160m. Completed: one small bug fix (counts as 0.5 M), started PR for telemetry extraction (in progress). CL: 4.
- 2026-02-24 (Wed) — Day 3: slipped on morning ritual (meeting bleed). Focus minutes 95. Need better meeting buffer. Note: Pomodoro 25/5 tried mid-block — felt disjointed for deep modeling tasks.
- 2026-03-01 (Mon) — End week 1 summary: M=1.5 (bug fix + half PR), avg F=135. Streak=3 (good). Retrospect: morning ritual helps clarify but calendar conflicts kill the second block.
- 2026-03-08 (Mon) — End week 2 summary: M=2 (merged PR #642), avg F=145. Streak=6. CL down to 3 median. Thought: Small wins stacking.
- 2026-03-10 (Wed) — Mid-sprint micro-retro: adjust reward — swap email to Maya for short Slack check-in (less overhead). Test: can I move second block to 16:00–17:30 to avoid recurring meetings?

What worked:
- Morning chunking forces priorities — less flail at 11am.
- Protected blocks increase deep work output when uninterrupted.
- Weekly externalization (Eliot) gives small accountability boost.

What didn't work / open problems:
- Meetings are the biggest leak; recurring team syncs often expand. Need to negotiate hard boundaries.
- Pomodoro (25/5) is not universally helpful — for model tuning it's disruptive. Might be good for triage tasks only.
- Measurement gaps: GH label automation missed one merged PR due to tag mismatch (fix script).

Immediate actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Add 'owner:jasper' tag rule to PR template (GH PR template) — link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-templates/pull/xx (TODO file issue).
- [ ] Update Clockify project tags to include 'habit-experiment' and make daily export cron job (Eliot agreed to help).
- [ ] Block calendar 14:30–15:30 on Wednesdays as meeting buffer.
- [ ] Write short note to team about focus-block etiquette (draft in Slack #eng-focus).

Hypotheses for A/B within Sprint
A: Morning ritual + 2x90-min blocks + social accountability via Slack -> higher M than B.
B: Morning ritual + 1x120-min block + evening wrap -> similar M but lower subjective fatigue.
Plan: run A in odd weeks, B in even weeks. Track subjective fatigue in EOD notes (1–5 scale).

Risks and signals to stop:
- If M does not increase after 3 sprints AND CL increases -> abort and change approach.
- If focus minutes F increase but M does not -> signal wasted busy-work; inspect task selection.

Notes to self (shorthand)
- Keep interventions as light as possible. Avoid 'optimization theater' 
- Share one short metric chart with manager at next 1:1 (M, F, S, CL trend)
- Be flexible: the goal is sustainable increase in meaningful output, not maximal hours.

Linked references / quick links:
- PR automation script (gist): https://github.com/redwood-inference/personal-habit-gists/gist1234
- Confluence template for micro-retro: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=98765
- Slack etiquette draft: https://slack.com/archives/C02ENG/pm12345

End of scratchpad. Will update nightly (EOD short bullets) and summarize weekly for sprint retro.

— Jasper
